summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would expand online gambling regulation to cover games where players gamble using virtual items that have been bought with real money.
It would change the Interactive Gambling Act 2001 definition of gambling service so items of value expressly included virtual items purchased in or connected with games.
The new definition would take effect 28 days after Royal Assent and address gambling activities involving virtual purchases made using real currency.
changes: The statutory gambling service definition would be amended.
Virtual purchases made within a game or in relation to it would fall within the specified items of value.
The new definition would apply after the 28-day commencement period.
summary.affected: Players gambling with purchased virtual items and providers of games offering those activities are affected.

speeches.speaker: Nick Xenophon
speeches.brief: The Interactive Gambling Amendment (Virtual Credits) Bill 2013 was moved to close a loophole by redefining "gambling service" to include virtual tokens, credits, or coins purchased with real money, citing examples like DoubleDown Casino and Zynga Poker where consumers could not cash out winnings. The amendment aims to improve consumer protection and prevent children’s access to such games.
